DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: 
Will the Minister of SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether technological policy of 1983 promised that fullest support 
would be given to development of indigenous technology to achieve 
technological self-reliance in criti cal areas and in high value added 
items in which domestic base is strong; 
(b) if so, whether the scientific revolution of 20th century has made 
unprecedented impact on the economic growth and social development; 
(c) if so, whether Government's Science and Technology Policy of 
2003 has made a number of declarations; 
(d) to what extent it has given further improvement in technological 
policy; and 
(e) to what extent this new policy has been helpful to India's growth? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. The Scientific 
Policy Resolution of 1958 (SPR-1958) and the Technology Policy 
Statement of 1983 (TPS-1983) emph asized the important role of 
technology in national developmen t. Technological advancement and 
national development were identified as the primary objectives of scientific 
activities in the country. TPS-1983 was formulated in the pre-globalization 
era and it emphasized indigenous technology development for achieving 
self-reliance. 
The policy framework provided by SPR-1958 and TPS-1983, together 
with the scientific revolution of the 20th century, greatly helped in the 
social development and economic growth  of India. One can clearly notice 
several aspects of social devel opment since Independence which can 
directly be ascribed to significant sc ientific advances in the country. 
For example, the Green Revolution, the White Revolution, the 
developments in Nuclear, Space, Defence and DNA-based technologies, 
the advances in Drug Development, the Computer Software and IT 
40 

[12 May, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
Revolution and the Telecommunication Revolution. Compared to 1950, 
our GNP in now approximately 230 times, food grain production is now 
4 times, oilseeds production is now 4 times, milk production is now 5 
times, our exports are now 340 times higher and India is expected to 
sustain a reasonable growth rate in future also. Our industries have also 
become technologically competitive. For example, our strengths in the 
IT sector are well known; from a net importer of bulk drugs, we have 
become an exporter of bulk drugs and our successes in the automobile 
sector have been impressive. On the social front, our birth rate has 
gone down, our death rate has gone down, our life expectancy has 
considerably increased, several dreade d diseases have been eradicated, 
and so on. 
(c) Yes, Sir. Like the policy statements in the past, the Science and 
Technology Policy of 2003 (STP-2003) has also made a number of 
declarations so that the Indian S&T system can meet the challenges of 
the post-globalization era. 
(d) and (e) The attempt by the Government is to shift from policy to 
performance and ensure that Scie nce and Technology works for the 
benefit of the common man. As India has a competitive advantage in 
the emerging knowledge-eco nomy, there is a subtle shift of emphasis to 
ensure that India provides leadersihp through innovation. Public-Private 
Partnerships to synergize the strengths of the academic and R&D 
sectors, industry and the Government are being promoted. The 
Government is also laying great emphasis on human resource 
development and entrepreneurship.

Policy on exploration and mining of coal 
5273. SHRI S.P.M. SYED KHAN : Will the PRIME MINISTER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the existing policy of Government with regard to the exploration 
and mining of coal; 
69 

RAJYA SABHA [12 May, 2005] 
(b) the details regarding private participation in the coal sector in India, 
at present; 
(c) the production and monetary gain achieved through private 
participation during the last five years; and 
(d) whether Government would continue to support the private 
participation in the coal sector taking into account its experience in the 
matter? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL (DR. 
DASARI NARAYANA RAO): (a) Explorati on of coal is carried out in two 
stages, in the first stage, Geological  Survey of India (GSI) undertakes 
Regional Exploration for locating the potential coal bearing areas on a 
continuous basis from the fund provided by Ministry of Mines. Ministry of 
Coal supplements these efforts through the scheme of Promotional (Regional) 
Exploration on Plan to Plan basis. In the second stage, Detailed 
Exploration is carried out in potential block identified through Regional/ 
Promotional Exploration from the funds provided by coal companies for 
blocks retained by them. For detailed exploration in other blocks, not to 
be retained by subsidiaries of Coal India Limited, Ministry of Coal provides 
fund on Plan to Plan basis. 
As regards policy of mining of coal, coal mining continues in the 
public sector except for captive mining purposes. State Government 
companies or undertakings are also allowed to do mining of coking and 
non-coking coal or lignite reserves, either by opencast or underground 
method, any where in the country, subject to certain conditions. 
(b) At*resent, the participation of private sector is limited to mining 
of coal for captive consumption in specified end uses only. 
(c) Coal production by captive collieries during the year 2003-04 
was about 11.22 million tonnes. 
(d) Private sector participation in commercial mining would be feasible 
only when the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973 is amended. An 
amendment Bill namely, the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Amendment 
Bill 2000 was introduced in the Rajya Sabha in April, 2000 that seeks, 
inter alia, to allow Indian companies to undertake exploration as well as 
to mine coal and lignite for commercial purposes.

External Affairs Minister (EAM) met King Gyanendera of Nepal on the 
sidelines of the Asian African Summit in Jakarta on April 22,2005. During 
the meeting, EAM stressed the need for release of political leaders, lifting of 
emergency and media censorship and resumption of process of 
reconciliation between political parties and the constitutional monarchy lead- 
ing to the restoration of multi-party democracy in Nepal. EAM also con- 
veyed India's strong belief that the problems confronting Nepal,

declaration of the emergency in Nepal and outlined the steps that he had 
already taken to remove some of the restrictions. He conveyed his 
intention to lift the emergency and restore democratic processes in Nepal.

release of all political leaders still in custody and the restoration of civil

Reduction of poverty level 
5360. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR: Will the PRIME MINISTER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have fixed any target for reduction of poverty 
level; 
(b) if so, the target fixed during the Ninth Five Year Plan period and the 
actual target achieved; 
(c) the target fixed for the Tenth Five Year Plan; and 
(d) the specific steps being taken by Government in this direction? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING 
(SHRI M.V. RAJASEKHARAN): (a) Yes, Sir. The Government in the Tenth 
Plan Period (2002-2007) have set a target for reduction of poverty by 5 
percentage point by 2007 and by 15 percentage point by 2012. 
(b) There was no target fixed for reduction of poverty level in the Ninth 
Plan period. 
(c) Consistent with the overall growth target of 8% per annum and its 
State-wise distribution as given in th e Plan, the Tenth Five Year (2002-07) 
Plan for the first time has set a target for reduction of poverty by 5 
percentage 
point by 2007 and by 15 percentage point by 2012. 
(d) The Government has adopted a three pronged strategy for reducing 
poverty: (i) acceleration of economic growth with a focus on sectors which 
are employment intensive; (ii) human and social development through 
provision of basic minimum services; and (iii) targeted anti-poverty 
programmes. 
The programmes which are being implemented in the rural areas by 
Ministry of Rural Development for upliftment of BPL families are 
(i) Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana  (SGRY), (ii) Swaranjayanti Gram 
Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY), (iii) Indira Awas Yojana(IAY) and (iv) National 
Food for Works Programme(NFFWP). 
The programme which is being implemented in the urban areas for 
169 

RAJYA SABHA [12 May, 2005] 
poverty alleviation is Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rojgar Yojana (SJSRY). The 
programme targets the urban poor, defined as those living Below the Poverty 
Line, as defined from time to time. The Programme is applicable to all 
urban towns in India. The Programme is implemented on a whole town 
basis with special emphasis on urban poor clusters. In addition to this, 
the Valmiki Ambedkar Awas Yojana (VAMBAY), and National Slum 
Development Programmes (NSDP) which are meant for providing shelter/ 
upgradation of shelter and environmental upgradation for the urban slum 
dwellers, also contribute indirectly towards poverty alleviation. 
In addition, under the new shceme of the Targeted Public Distribution 
System (TPDS) each poor family is entitled to 35 kgs of foodgrains. In 
order to make the TPDS more focused and targeted towards the very poor 
category, the "Antyodaya Anna Yojana" provides 35 kgs of foodgrains to 
the poorest of the poor families at a highly subsidized rate of Rs. 2 per 
kg., for wheat and Rs. 3 per kg., for rice.  In the recent budget presented on 
28-02-05 it was announced that the coverage of Antyodaya Anna Yojana 
will be increased from 2.0 crore (BPL) families to 2.5 crore families in 
2005.

Empowering women through TREAD 
5405. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the Minister of SMALL SCALE 
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that his Mini stry has started a scheme called 
TREAD to empower women economically throagh the development of their 
entrepreneual skills; 
(b) if so, the details of the scheme; and 
(c) the number of women entrepreneur s assisted through this scheme 
since its inception, State-wise? 
213 

RAJYA SABHA [12 May, 2005] 
THE MINISTER OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES (SHRI MAHABIR 
PRASAD): (a) The Government in the Ministry of Small Scale Industries 
has been operating a scheme titled "Trade Related Entrepreneurship 
Assistance and Development" (TREAD ) for Women for their empowerment 
through the development of their entrepreneurial skills in non-farm activities. 
(b) The three main components of this scheme are as under: 
(i) Assistance in the form of the Government of India (Gol) grant of up to 
30% of the total project cost, as appraised by the lending agencies, is 
provided to the Non Governmental Organizations (NGOs) for grant activities 
and for capacity building of NGOs promoting entrepreneurship among target 
groups of women. 
(ii) Training institutions and NGOs ca n avail of Gol grant of up to Rs. 
1.00 lakh per programme, for imparting training to the women entrepreneurs, 
provided such institutions also bring their share of at least 25% of the 
grant. 
(iii) Need-based Government grant of up to Rs. 5 lakh per project is 
provided to Entrepreneurship Developm ent Institutions (EDIs) primarily for 
undertaking field surveys, research studies, evaluation studies, designing 
of training modules, etc. 
(c) The state wise number of women assisted under this scheme is as 
under:

Modernisation of Statistical System 
5407. SHRI K. KAMARAJ: Will the Minister of STATISTICS AND 
PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Governme nt are considering to modernise 
the statistical system with World Bank support; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that the statistical details presently recorded 
to not reflect the actual position with regard to production and consumption; 
and 
218 

[12 May, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(d) if so, the steps taken to improve the data base? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS 
AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION (SHRI OSCAR 
FERNANDES): (a) and (b) The World Bank has agreed to support the 
following studies under the Scheme Technical Assistance for Economic 
Reforms' for modernisation of statistical system in the country: 
(i) Establishment of an All India Statistical Network. 
(ii) Identifying the Specific Requirements of Strengthening of the State 
Directorates of Economics and Statistics. 
(iii) Creation and Maintenance of a Business Register. 
(iv) Improvement of Service Sector Statistics. 
(v) Assessing the Survey Capabilities of Private Sector. 
(c) and (d) Production and consumption in the economy are estimated 
on the basis of statistics available from various administrative sources and 
surveys conducted following scientific methods so as to make the estimates 
as reliable as possible. However, improvement of statistical system is a 
continuous process. Steps taken in this regard include launching of India 
Statiscal Strengthening Project, Strengthening of data processing 
capabilities, Traning of statistical officers, Conducting economic census, 
Adoption of international standards in statistical activities, Preparation of 
standard manuals on different subjects of official statistics, etc.

†5414. PROF. M.M. AGARWAL: Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have formulated any effective scheme to give 
boost to sports in the country; 
(b) the funds allocated for the devel opment of Sports during the years 
2002-03,2003-04 and 2004-05, State-wise; and 
(c) the names of sports projects completed with the help of funds provided 
to States during the said period? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL 
DUTT): (a) With a view to give boost to sports in the country, the following 
broad schemes are being implemented by the Ministry: 
(i) Scheme of Incentive for Promotion of Sports Activities. 
Under this scheme, financial assistance is provided for Promotion of 
Sports & Games in Schools and Rural Sports Programmes. Pension to- 
Meritorius Sportspersons and Sports Scholarship are also provided. Under 
this Scheme, the Ministry operates the National Sports Development Fund 
to mobilise funds through donations for Promotion of Sports. 
(ii) Scheme Relating to Awards. 
Under this Scheme, Sportspersons who show excellence at National & 
International level are considered for Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award. 
Special Awards to Winners in Internatio nal Sports Events and their coaches 
are also given. Maulana Abul Kalam A zad Trophy is given to the winner of 
the Inter University Tournaments. 
Apart from the above. Arjuna, Dhyanchand and Dronacharya Awards 
are also given to current and former  Sportspersons and coaches for their 
achievements in the field of sports. 
(iii) Scheme Relating to Talent Search and Training. 
(iv) Scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations. 
(v) Scheme of Institutions.

programmes and schemes of Sports Authority of India and Lakshmibai 
National Institute of Physical Education. 
(vi) Scheme of State Sports Academies. 
(vii) Scheme for Dope Test. 
(viii) National Sports Championship for Women. 
(ix) National welfare Fund for Sportspersons. 
In addition, Sports Authority of India is also implementing the Schemes 
for Promotion of Sports namely (i) National Sports Talent Context; (ii) Army 
Boys Sports Company; (iii) Special Area Games; (iv) SAI Training Centres; 
and (v) Centres for Excellence

Bringing Sports in the concurrent list 
5415. SHRIMATI PREMA CARIAPPA : Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are considering to put sports in the concurrent 
list; 
(b) if so, whether all the State Governments have been consulted in this 
regard; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL 
DUTT): (a) Yes, Sir. A proposal for transfer of subject of "Sports" from the 
'State List' to the 'Concurrent List' of the Constitution of India was initiated 
by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports in 1988. A Constitution (61st 
Amendment) Bill was introduced in the Rajya Sabha in November, 1988, 
and is still pending there. 
(b) and (c) The State Governments were consulted on the proposal. A 
large number of States had agreed to the proposed transfer of the subject 
of "Sports" from the 'State List' to the 'Concurrent List' of the Constitution 
of India. However, this issue was also discussed in the Conference of 
Sports Ministers and State Secretar ies held on 16.2.2005 in New Delhi 
where it was indicated by the represen tatives of State Governments that 
they would take a view on the subject and send their written communication 
in this regard.

GOVERNMENT BILLS 
The Right to Information Bill, 2005. 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, 
PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS AND MINISTER OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS (SHRI SURESH PACHOURI): Sir, I beg to 
move: 
That the Bill to provide for setting out  the practical regime of right to 
information for people to secure access to information under the control 
of public authorities, in order  to promote transparency and 
accountability in the working of ever y public authority, the constitution 
of a Central Information Commission and for matters connected 
therewith or incidental thereto, as passed by Lok Sabha, be taken into 
consideration.  
    Sir, I rise to urge the support and appr oval of the House to this Bill, which is 
a significant landmark in the evolution of the right to information. This Bill 
promises to make this right to inform ation more progressive, participatory and

The preamble states inter alia the expediency to provide information to

The procedure of securing information as provided in clause 6 of this 
Bill prescribes a procedure which intent ionally has been kept very simple. 
A citizen has to merely make a request to the concerned Public Information

information. In case the person is unable to make the request in writing, 
the Public Information Offi cer is required to render  assistance to him in

Įी उपसभापित : शुिक्रया । Įी जयराम रमेश। 
SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH: Sir, I will make just three points. One, Mr. 
Nariman's fears, echoed by Mrs. Bachchan, are totally misplaced. All the 
information, which our rivals or our co mpetitors want, they have. Thus, for 
us to assume that somebody is going to use this Act to get the informa- 
tion, I think, is living in a fool's paradise. Let's be under no illusions. Those 
people who want information about us, do get it. A classic example is, 
photographs of our airports, which is prohibited by Indian law, is available 
if you go to some websites. Photogra phs of every Indian airport are freely 
available elsewhere. 
Secondly, Sir, having been associated with this legislation from day 
one, I want to make one special plea to the hon. Minister. As far I was 
concerned I looked upon this Bill as not to empower the media, not to 
empower business rivals, but really to empower the local-self government 
institutions, the panchayati raj institutions. I was inspired for this legislation 
by the example of the Mazdoor-Kisan Sang harsh Samiti of Rajasthan, 
which has used Rajasthan's Freedom of Information Act to impose 
accountability in rural development programmes, and improve their 
implementation. So, there is a very close connection between what we 
are doing today and panchayati raj and rural development. And, in fact, my 
original suggestion was that this Bill should have been piloted by the 
Ministry of Panchayati Raj. But that  did not happen. I would still appeal to 
the hon. Minister to bring this legislat ion and weave it into the mainstream 
of rural development and panchayati raj institutions, because that is the 
main reason why we are bringing forward this legislation, and not to satisfy 
some middle class curiosity. 
Finally, Sir, the problem in our system  is the culture of secrecy. There 
is a cult of secrecy in our system, and the starting point of this cult is the 
Third Schedule of the Constitution. It is the oath of secrecy. The hon. Mr. 
Suresh Pachouri has taken the oath of  secrecy. I want him to take the 
oath of transparency. I think, if the U PA Government were to replace the oath 
of secrecy from Ministers with an oath of transparency, this example will 
percolate and this Bill will then begin to have some effect. Thank you, Sir.

The Bihar Value Added Tax Bill, 2005 
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Now, we will take up the Bihar Value Added 
Tax Bill, 2005. Mr. P. Chidambaram to move the Bill. 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): Sir, I beg to 
move: 
"That the Bill to consolidate and amend the law relating to levy of tax on 
sales or purchases of goods in the Stat e of Bihar and to provide for matters 
connected therewith or incidential t hereto, as passed by Lok Sabha, be 
taken into consideration." 
Sir, the Bihar Value Added Tax B ill, 2005 seeks to  consolidate and 
amend the law relating to levy of tax on sales or purchases of goods. This 
is a State level Value Added Tax which replaces the sales tax being levied 
earlier. Tax on sale or purchase of goods is a State subject under entry 52 
of the State list. As part of the tax reform process it was decided in the 
Conference of Chief Ministers held in November, 1999 to introduce VAT. 
An Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers was also constituted 
to monitor the process of introduction of VAT. The Empowered Committee 
on 18th June, 2004 recommended that State level VAT should be 
implemented with effect from 1st April, 2005. 
361 

RAJYA SABHA [12 May, 2005] 
Twenty-three States and UTs hav e already introduced the State- 
level VAT. The remaining States and UTs are expected to introduce it 
shortly. 
The Governor of Bihar promulgat ed the Bihar VAT Ordinance on the 4th 
March, 2005. Accordingly,  the VAT has been introduced in Bihar w.e.f. 1st 
April, 2005. 
On 7th March, 2005, the State of Bihar came under President's Rule 
Article 356 of the Constitution. As per this Article, the powers of the State 
legislature of Bihar shall be exerci sable by or under the authority of 
Parliament. Therefore, the Bihar VAT Ordinance has to be replaced by an 
Act to be passed by Parliament. 
Sir, the VAT is a modern, simple an d transparent tax system which has 
been found beneficial throughout the world.  This is a single most important 
tax reform undertaken in India. 
I would urge the hon. Members to pass the Bill. Thank you.
